outcome.technical: DONE. Re-recorded .github/sweep-costs.json from the three plain Windows selftests legs of CI run 40549328014 at e236bb23. Logs 122348471060 (shard 1/3), 122348471282 (2/3) and 122348471362 (3/3) were checked by the `verify.sh --only selftests --shard I/3` line in each, then concatenated. The command was `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <scratchpad>/p14225-plain-legs.log --platform windows-latest --workers 4 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`, exit 0, and it printed `recorded 193 files' seconds ... (windows-latest)`. `--costs-from-log` takes ONE log, so several are concatenated, as ci.yml's comment says. A file printed twice keeps its longest timing. `windows-latest` matches the existing table and ci.yml. Every swept file is now timed (193 of 193; the old table timed 177). Split-file figures, old -> new: test_drive_phase 1346.4 -> 4615.2, test_audit_task 606.0 -> 1069.3, test_commit_task_work 222.9 -> 764.5, test_stamp_verification 265.4 -> 540.5, test_close_phase 330.3 -> 448.0, test__deps 268.2 -> 323.4, test__output 177.2 -> 24.7, check-committed-pii 83.1 -> 83.1. ADDED case swd7 to tests/test_stamp_verification.py in `_sweep_deadline_cases`, block swd-block. It rewrites the committed table with the sweep's own `record_costs` from the table's own figures, platform and workers, and requires the result to be byte for byte the committed file. It was red on the old table (shown above) and is green now. Gate `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_stamp_verification.py` exit 0, `1/1 files ok, 325 cases`. `ruff check tests/test_stamp_verification.py` exit 0. ABOUT TEXT: yes. The re-record writes `record_costs`'s current `about` text, so the table now carries exactly the text P142.29 asked for, and swd7 holds it byte for byte. P142.29 declares the same table and test file, so a case it adds for the about text would duplicate swd7. RESOLUTION CONFIRMATIONS, BOTH NOT MET. (1) The split is not balanced. Computed with the sweep's own `shard_paths` over `sweep_files()` (script <scratchpad>/p14225-split.py, exit 0): shard 1/3 = 1 file, test_drive_phase.py, 4615.2 slot-s; 2/3 = 96 files, 2830.0; 3/3 = 96 files, 2830.0. At file granularity no split can do better: that one suite is more than a third of the tree's total. The old table's split read 1681.5/1681.5/1681.4 on stale figures. Its real plain-leg step walls in this run (log timestamps, verify step start to VERIFY OK) were 21m30s for 1/3 against 11m33s and 11m25s. (2) Every split file's timeout at held=3 sits within 2x of its figure, and no re-record can change that. `file_timeout` at held = stage_grant(4) = 3 is ceil(TIMEOUT_PER_COST 3 x figure / 3) = the figure itself whenever that is over the 300 s floor. Ratio timeout/figure = 1.00 for test__deps, test_audit_task, test_close_phase, test_commit_task_work, test_drive_phase and test_stamp_verification; 12.15 for test__output and 3.61 for check-committed-pii, both on the floor. The process that timeout bounds is one block. Against the per-block MEAN (figure / blocks) the timeout is at least 11.0x (test__deps, the lowest). The CI log prints no per-block seconds, so the per-block MAXIMUM is unmeasured. REGRESSION THE RE-RECORD CAUSES, IN A FILE NOT MINE: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --selftest` exit 1, `139/140`, with `FAIL tt5 ... deadline 1380s + setup 120s vs 26 minutes; longest file timeout 4616s`. On the HEAD table that figure is 1347, under 1380, so tt5 was green. Each block of test_drive_phase is given the whole suite's slot-seconds as its timeout, which now exceeds SWEEP_DEADLINE. Both failures point at tools/sweep-selftests.py, outside this task's files, and I did not edit it. The fix is a design change, not data. A block's timeout should be calibrated from its own share (work_items already estimates a block as figure / blocks) rather than the whole file's sum. Sharding should be able to divide a staged suite's blocks across shards, or that suite's cost has to come down. Recommend a tracked task or fault for this before sign-off. MEASURED SPREAD, one run only: across the plain and cp1252 legs of run 40549328014, files of at least 20 s varied by up to 2.19x (test__refs 32.4 vs 14.8, tools/affected.py 30.7 vs 15.2, test_drive_phase 4615.2 vs 2781.0). The comment above TIMEOUT_PER_COST in tools/sweep-selftests.py records at most 1.51x for the earlier runs, so it is out of date; the factor of 3 still covers this spread. That file's comment naming test_drive_phase at 1347s is also out of date. DEPENDANTS. .github/sweep-costs.json -> .github/workflows/ci.yml: still correct; its re-record recipe is the command run here. Its `resample` estimate (13m30s, no run yet) was derived on the old figures, and two drawn suites grew (test_stamp_verification 265.4 -> 540.5, test_run_test_gate 85.4 -> 159.1), so the estimate is probably low; the job's bound is 40 min. -> plugins/audit/scripts/governance/stamp-verification.py: unchanged and still correct; it sizes the red-first deadline as 3x the named suites' figures, capped by the host limit, so those deadlines grow with the new figures. -> tests/test_stamp_verification.py: changed by this task (swd7); swd5 still green, still reading the same table. -> tools/sweep-selftests.py: NOT still correct. tt5 is red, the split changed as above, and two comments are out of date. -> CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: still correct; they name the table and the command and carry no figure from it (grep for 1346/1347/sweep-costs). tools/check-committed-pii.py: not changed. `python3 tools/check-committed-pii.py` exit 0; its domain is evidence, journal, plan, report and return, not .github. A grep of the new table for a backslash, C:/, /Users/ or runneradmin found nothing. Its dependants are therefore still correct, and so are the names it defines that are used elsewhere. tests/test_stamp_verification.py's names used elsewhere (_crlf_cases, _scan) are untouched.
